```{python}
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from _showcase import load_metrics  # noqa: E402
from IPython.display import HTML, display  # noqa: E402

m = load_metrics()

# Honest numbers, straight from the committed metrics.json (placeholders if the harness hasn't run).
if m:
    a = m["aggregate"]
    n_skills = len(m.get("skills", {})) or 1
    stuck = f"{a['preferences_stuck']}<span style='color:var(--ws-text-faint)'>/{a['preferences_total']}</span>"
    rts = f"{a['median_runs_to_stick']:g}"
    scenarios = str(a["scenarios"])
    skills_n = str(n_skills)
else:
    stuck = rts = scenarios = skills_n = "&mdash;"

stat_tiles = f"""
<div class="ws-stats" style="max-width:820px;margin-inline:auto;">
  <div class="ws-stat"><div class="ws-stat-num"><span class="ws-accent">{stuck}</span></div>

  <div class="ws-stat"><div class="ws-stat-num">{rts}</div>
    <div class="ws-stat-label">median runs to stick</div></div>

    <div class="ws-stat-label">skills across 3 classes</div></div>
  <div class="ws-stat"><div class="ws-stat-num">{scenarios}</div>
    <div class="ws-stat-label">real scenarios measured</div></div>
</div>
"""

display(HTML(f"""
<section class="ws-hero">
  <span class="ws-eyebrow">local · open source · MCP</span>

  <p class="ws-hero-sub">Whetstone is a local <a href="https://modelcontextprotocol.io">MCP</a> server

    <a class="ws-btn ws-btn-primary" href="#get-started">Get started &rarr;</a>

    </div>

  {stat_tiles}
</section>
"""))
```

```{=html}
<section class="ws-section ws-section--alt">

      There is no LLM judge grading &ldquo;prettiness.&rdquo; The point is to show a correction is

      produced.
    </p>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="ws-section">
  <div class="ws-wrap">
    <div class="ws-reveal">
      <span class="ws-eyebrow">how it works</span>
      <h2 class="ws-section-title">Cold, corrected, then warm</h2>
      <p class="ws-section-lead">Whetstone turns an ordinary correction into a durable, weighted
        memory the skill reads back on its next run.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="ws-steps ws-reveal">
      <div class="ws-step">
        <div class="ws-step-title">Cold</div>
        <p class="ws-step-body">The skill runs with an empty store. The house-style preference you
          care about is usually <em>not</em> honored — that&rsquo;s the baseline.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="ws-step">
        <div class="ws-step-title">Capture</div>
        <p class="ws-step-body">You correct the skill. <code>capture</code> records it as a weighted
          <strong>learning</strong> (soft taste) or a mandatory <strong>issue</strong> (hard rule),
          committed to git.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="ws-step">
        <div class="ws-step-title">Warm</div>
        <p class="ws-step-body"><code>recall</code> injects the relevant learned layer at the start of
          the next run. The preference is honored — and stays honored.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

```{python}
# | echo: false
# | output: asis
# Proof cards + the skills covered — data-driven so the copy can never drift from metrics.json.
SKILL_META = {
    "great-tables": ("Great Tables", "Publication-ready data tables"),
    "frontend-design": ("Frontend design", "Self-contained web pages"),
    "plotnine": ("plotnine", "Grammar-of-graphics plots"),
    "pptx": ("PowerPoint decks", "python-pptx presentations"),
}


def skill_cards(metrics):
    skills = (metrics or {}).get("skills", {})
    order = list(SKILL_META) + [s for s in skills if s not in SKILL_META]
    cards = []
    for key in order:
        if key not in skills:
            continue
        label, blurb = SKILL_META.get(key, (key, ""))
        s = skills[key]
        n = s.get("scenarios", "?")
        cards.append(
            f'<div class="ws-card"><h3 class="ws-card-title">{label}</h3>'
            f'<p class="ws-card-body">{blurb}</p>'
            f'<span class="ws-card-more">{n} scenario{"s" if n != 1 else ""} '
            f'· {s.get("preferences_stuck", "?")}/{s.get("preferences_total", "?")} stuck</span></div>'
        )
    return "".join(cards) or '<p class="ws-section-lead">Skills appear once the harness has run.</p>'


display(HTML(f"""
<section class="ws-section ws-section--alt">
  <div class="ws-wrap">
    <div class="ws-reveal">

      <p class="ws-section-lead">Two independent views of the same claim, across every skill.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="ws-cards ws-reveal">

        <span class="ws-card-more">See it &rarr;</span>
      </a>
      <a class="ws-card" href="metrics.html">
        <div class="ws-card-icon">▤</div>
        <h3 class="ws-card-title">Metrics</h3>
        <p class="ws-card-body">Runs-to-stick and value-over-time, read straight from Whetstone&rsquo;s
          telemetry — never hand-set.</p>
        <span class="ws-card-more">Measure it &rarr;</span>
      </a>
      <a class="ws-card" href="methodology.html">
        <div class="ws-card-icon">◆</div>
        <h3 class="ws-card-title">Methodology</h3>
        <p class="ws-card-body">Exactly how every number on this site is produced, and what &ldquo;honored&rdquo;
          means for each preference.</p>
        <span class="ws-card-more">Read it &rarr;</span>
      </a>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="ws-section">
  <div class="ws-wrap">
    <div class="ws-reveal">
      <span class="ws-eyebrow">breadth</span>
      <h2 class="ws-section-title">One substrate, many skills</h2>
      <p class="ws-section-lead">The same attach / recall / capture / revise loop drives every skill —
        only the skill and the taught preference change.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="ws-cards ws-reveal">
      {skill_cards(m)}
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
"""))
```

```{=html}
        <p class="ws-card-body">A preference you hold across skills — &ldquo;muted palettes, never
          neon&rdquo; — is promoted once and recalled everywhere, origin-tagged so the specific still
          wins.</p>
        <span class="ws-card-more">Concept &rarr;</span>
```
